item.name: POST Mint a short-lived, JWKS-signed access JWT (token_use:api_key, jti) whose exp is clamped to the smallest of the req

request.description:
Mint a short-lived, JWKS-signed access JWT (token_use:api_key, jti) whose exp is clamped to the smallest of the request, the key expiry and the org ceiling; scopes + constraints are embedded so a resource verifies it OFFLINE against the instance JWKS. When the key registered a public_key, the token also carries cnf.jkt (proof-of-possession) and a resource additionally checks a holder-signed proof. Authenticate with (1) an sk_ bearer + the ak_ in the body, (2) an Authorization: Bearer ak_… that self-mints for itself, or (3) no bearer + x-publishable-key naming the instance with the ak_ in the body. A key only ever mints within its own instance. The api_keys:read scope applies ONLY to the sk_ path; the ak_ and publishable-key paths are self-scoped.
**Required scope:** `api_keys:read`

`POST /v1/api_keys/token`

item.name: POST Mint an end-user API key for a user, organization or machine (returns the ak_ secret once), OR import an existing k

request.description:
Mint an end-user API key for a user, organization or machine (returns the ak_ secret once), OR import an existing key by its SHA-256 hash (hash_algorithm "sha256" or "sha256_hex") so it verifies against the original secret. Normally authenticated with an sk_ key; a LAN/offline MACHINE may instead self-provision a key for ITSELF by presenting Authorization: Bearer <machine JWT> (token_use:m2m from /v1/machines/token) + x-publishable-key — the subject is forced to that machine and it cannot grant itself management-plane scopes. Pass public_key (an SPKI PEM) to make the key proof-of-possession: tokens minted from it carry cnf.jkt and a resource verifies a holder-signed proof OFFLINE.
**Required scope:** `api_keys:write`

`POST /v1/api_keys`

Pass a stable `device_key` to make this a RE-ENROLMENT: the device's previous machine registration is superseded (revoked, emitting machine.revoked reason 'superseded') across ANY enrolment token in the instance/org before the cap is checked — so a device moving to a different token takes over its own slot instead of counting twice. Enrolment is capped at the SMALLER of the token's `max_machines` and the owning org plan's device limit (the entitlement `max_machines`/`max_devices`); exceeding either is a 403 naming the bound that was hit. A supersede spends no extra use.

`POST /v1/machines/enroll`
